summary:
CanSat Monitoring is an interactive educational and engineering platform that brings together CanSat design, electronics, programming, flight simulation, and telemetry monitoring in one virtual environment. It helps students and aspiring engineers understand the complete lifecycle of a small satellite mission, from selecting electronic components and designing circuits to simulating flight stages and analyzing mission data.

The platform provides a virtual laboratory for assembling electronic systems, a circuit design environment, a programming workspace, a 3D simulation concept, and a monitoring dashboard for visualizing parameters such as altitude, GPS coordinates, velocity, temperature, and atmospheric pressure.

By making aerospace engineering concepts more accessible and interactive, CanSat Monitoring supports practical STEM education and encourages experimentation without requiring every physical component or flight test. It connects engineering decisions with mission outcomes and helps users better understand how small satellite systems work.
details:
Project Overview

CanSat Monitoring is an interactive platform designed to support the learning, development, testing, and monitoring of CanSat (Can-sized Satellite) systems. The project combines electronics, programming, aerospace engineering, 3D visualization, and telemetry technologies to create a unified digital environment for educational space mission development.

The main goal is to make the CanSat mission development process more accessible by allowing users to explore the engineering workflow before or alongside building a physical device.

How It Works

The platform is organized around several interconnected modules:

1. Virtual Laboratory

Users can explore electronic components, microcontrollers, sensors, and connection elements in a virtual workspace. This environment helps them understand how electronic systems can be assembled before physical implementation.

2. Circuit Designer

The circuit design module allows users to select electronic components, connect sensors and modules, and visualize relationships between microcontroller pins and other electronic elements. It helps users understand the structure of a CanSat electronic system.

3. Programming Environment

The programming module is intended for developing control algorithms, processing sensor readings, and defining device behavior. It connects the software logic with the electronic system design.

4. 3D Simulation Environment

The 3D simulation concept visualizes important stages of a CanSat mission, including rocket launch, separation, descent, parachute deployment, and landing. It helps users understand the sequence of a mission and observe the device's movement in a virtual environment.

5. Monitoring Dashboard

The monitoring dashboard presents mission telemetry through numerical indicators and visual charts. Relevant parameters include altitude, GPS coordinates, velocity, temperature, atmospheric pressure, descent profile, and signal strength.

6. GPS Tracking

The geographic tracking module uses location coordinates to display the device's position, movement path, and estimated landing location on a map.

Benefits and Intended Impact

CanSat Monitoring aims to make aerospace engineering and satellite technology more accessible to students, educators, and beginner engineers.

Its main benefits include:

  • Providing an interactive environment for learning aerospace engineering concepts.
  • Connecting electronics, programming, simulation, and telemetry in one platform.
  • Helping users understand the relationship between engineering decisions and mission performance.
  • Supporting virtual experimentation before physical testing.
  • Making telemetry easier to understand through charts, maps, and visual indicators.
  • Encouraging interest in STEM education, satellite technology, and scientific exploration.

Creativity and Innovation

The creative aspect of CanSat Monitoring is its integrated approach. Instead of treating electronics, programming, flight simulation, and telemetry as separate learning activities, the platform brings them together into one connected workflow.

Users can explore the process of designing a CanSat system, preparing its electronic architecture, developing control logic, observing simulated mission stages, and analyzing telemetry data.

This approach turns abstract aerospace engineering concepts into an interactive learning experience.

Technologies and Tools

The project description includes the following technologies as part of its proposed technical architecture:

  • Frontend: React.js
  • Backend: Python and FastAPI
  • Database: PostgreSQL
  • Real-time communication: WebSocket
  • 3D simulation: Unity
  • 3D modeling: Blender
  • Electronics and microcontrollers: Arduino and ESP32
  • Sensors: GPS, BMP280, and MPU6050
  • Telemetry communication: LoRa and RF
  • Data visualization: Chart.js or ECharts
  • Geographic visualization: Leaflet or Mapbox

Only technologies actually used in the submitted implementation should be considered part of the completed project.

Engineering Considerations

The project considers component selection, electronic connections, sensor data, microcontroller programming, device movement, telemetry transmission, and visualization of mission parameters.

The platform is intended to support a modular architecture so that additional sensors, electronic components, simulation scenarios, and monitoring capabilities can be introduced over time.

Future Development

Future improvements may include real-time synchronization between physical CanSat hardware and the virtual simulation, automated telemetry analysis, anomaly detection, support for multiple CanSat devices, and automatic mission reports.

CanSat Monitoring aims to make learning about small satellite systems more practical, visual, and accessible.
